newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-Feb energy consumption grows 8.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-Feb energy consumption grows 8.4 pct.

text.p: Electrical energy consumption in Brazil rose 8.4 percent to 45,331.2 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in the first two months versus January-February 1996, federal power firm Eletrobras said.
An Eletrobras spokeswoman said energy consumption during the 12 months ending in February rose 6.6 percent to 261,864.1 GWh compared with the prior 12-month period.
The rise in both industrial and residential power usage stems from a surge in electrical appliance purchases, increased industrial activity and new public works projects, she said.
"The economy is growing," she added. "It has to do with the Real (economic stabilization) plan."
March consumption figures were not immediately available, nor was the number of gigawatts consumed in January and February 1996.

Leading financial daily Gazeta Mercantil, meanwhile, said power consumption in the Sao Paulo area, Brazil's industrial heart, rose 3.8 percent in March to 7,201 gigawatt-hours versus the same month last year.
It did not give a comparative figure for March 1996.

A separate report said Brazil plans to spend 738 million reais to build a North-South transmission line to allow energy to flow along 1,270 kms from Imperatriz in the northeastern state of Maranhao to Samambaia near the capital of Brasilia.
Reports also said intends to buy 1,000 megawatts of power from Argentina to head off an expected energy shortfall.
